name: Cannabis tax rates by state
where_it_stands: States with adult-use sales tax cannabis on top of, or instead of, ordinary sales tax, using a percentage of price, a charge by weight, or a charge tied to THC content. Washington's 37% retail excise is the highest percentage rate, and several states changed rates in 2025 and 2026, including Connecticut's switch to a flat 10.75% on 1 October 2026.

next_milestone.text: Treasury and IRS guidance on Section 280E for medical operators, listed in the 2026-2027 Priority Guidance Plan; no release date has been set.

summary: State cannabis taxes come in three basic designs, according to the Tax Foundation. Most states charge a percentage of price at retail, wholesale or both: Washington levies a 37% retail excise, Montana 20% on adult-use sales, California a 15% excise, and New York a 9% state plus 4% local retail tax and a separate wholesale tax. Some tax by weight: Alaska charges growers $50 an ounce for mature flower, and Maine pairs a 14% sales tax with a per-pound cultivation tax that it cut on 1 January 2026. Others tie the rate to potency: Illinois charges 10% on flower at or below 35% THC, 25% above that and 20% on infused products, and Connecticut taxed by milligram of THC until replacing that with a flat 10.75% gross-receipts tax on 1 October 2026. Local taxes and regular sales taxes usually stack on top. There is no federal excise tax on cannabis, but Section 280E of the tax code denies normal deductions to businesses trafficking in Schedule I or II drugs; Treasury says it stopped applying to state-licensed medical marijuana from the 2026 tax year, while adult-use sellers remain covered.

what_changes.text: Shelf prices can carry several layers of tax; in high-tax states the combined rate can make legal products much pricier than illicit ones.
Wholesale and cultivation taxes are paid before retail, so rate changes ripple through contracts; potency-based taxes also add testing and compliance cost.
Rate changes such as Connecticut's flat tax and California's reversal of its 2025 increase move margins quickly, and 280E relief now applies only to medical activity.

timeline.event: California excise returns to 15% under AB 564
Maine cuts its per-pound cultivation excise and applies a 14% adult-use sales tax
Tax Foundation publishes its 2026 state cannabis tax comparison
Treasury says 280E relief for state-licensed medical marijuana applies from the 2026 tax year
Connecticut replaces its THC-per-milligram tax with a flat 10.75% tax

faq.q: Which state has the highest cannabis tax?
faq.a: Washington has the highest percentage rate, a 37% retail excise charged on top of sales tax. Illinois's 25% rate on flower above 35% THC is the highest potency-based rate.

faq.q: Is there a federal tax on cannabis?
faq.a: There is no federal cannabis excise tax. Section 280E raises effective income taxes by denying deductions to adult-use businesses.
Often less. Many states exempt registered patients from cannabis excise taxes, as Minnesota, Michigan and New Mexico do, though general sales tax may still apply.
